newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end morning session mixed.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end morning session mixed.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended Thursday morning mixed, as interest rate and property fears deterred investors from following Wall Street upwards.
The Hang Seng Index rose a marginal 11.92 points to 12,593.23, after see-sawing in a narrow range. Turnover was HK$4.496 billion, down on Wednesday morning's HK$5.63 billion.

"Basically, investors are taking a breather after yesterday's jump because the market's upside -- although it's there -- isn't unlimited," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager with Nikko Securities.
The Hang Seng surged 239.29 points on Wednesday.

"I think it (Wednesday's Hang Seng rise) was slightly overdone," said the head of trading at a Hong Kong brokerage, adding that it may have anticipated the Dow industrials' 92.71 point surge overnight.
The Hang Seng rose to a high of 12,635.52 just after the open before easing back in thin trade, see-sawing between shallow negative and positive territory for much of the morning.
Property stocks were sold after strong gains on Wednesday and the utility sector slipped, apparently on news HK Telecom planned to offer a discounted international direct dial service, brokers said.
Brokers and analysts said the discounts were seen as potentially hurting HK Telecom's margins.
HK Telecom fell HK$0.10 to HK$13.55, and fellow utility China Light slipped HK$0.30 to HK$34.60.
The properties sub-index was off 18.15 points at 21,953.49 points, and the utilities sub-index was down 53.07 points, or 0.51 percent, at 10,419.28.
Red chips also retreated slightly after recent strong rallies on the back of optimism about mainland asset injections.
"It's (just) profit-taking on red chips," said Elvic Ng, red chip analyst with Vickers Ballas.
Red chip Shanghai Industrial fell HK$0.40 to HK$39.70, and CITIC Pacific fell HK$0.10 to HK$39.20.
Among the banks, HSBC was up HK$0.50 at HK$187.00, and Dah Sing soared HK$0.80 to HK$32.00 and Wing Hang was up HK$0.667 at HK$28.50.
Among the property stocks, Great Eagle was off HK$0.60 at HK$23.20 and Sun Hung Kai Properties was down HK$0.50 at HK$77.50.
